extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants (or their agents) seeking accelerated examination at the German Patent and Trade Mark Office (DPMA) under the DPMA–CNIPA Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) pilot programme
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and eligibility criteria for filing a request for accelerated examination at the DPMA under the PPH pilot programme where the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) acts as Office of Earlier Examination (OEE). Covers required conditions, supporting documents, and procedural steps for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement a) Same earliest date (priority/filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the DPMA application on which PPH is requested and the OEE application(s) forming the basis of the PPH request shall have the same earliest date (whether this be a priority date or a filing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples are given as Case I–IV: (Case I) DPMA application validly claims priority from the OEE (Paris route); (Case II) DPMA application provides the basis of a valid priority claim for the OEE application; (Case III) applications share a common priority (including various PCT/national-phase and domestic/divisional permutations); (Case IV) PCT national phase application where both DPMA and OEE apps are derived from a common PCT international application having no priority claim. See annex figures A–L for route-specific examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement b) OEE determined one or more claims patentable/allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one corresponding OEE application has one or more claims that have been determined to be patentable by the OEE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are 'determined to be allowable/patentable' when the CNIPA examiner explicitly identified the claims to be allowable/patentable in the latest office action, even if a patent has not yet been granted. If an OEE office action does not explicitly state that a particular claim is allowable, those claims may be deemed implicitly allowable only if the applicant includes a declaration with the PPH request stating that 'no reason for rejection had been given in the CNIPA office action in relation to a claim and that this claim is therefore deemed to be allowable/patentable by the CNIPA.' Examples: claims not mentioned in the First Notice of the Opinion on Examination under the item concerning Claims, or in later Notices under the corresponding item, may be implicitly identified as allowable — in which case the declaration is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement c) All DPMA claims must sufficiently correspond to OEE-allowable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims in the DPMA application, as originally filed or as amended, for examination under the PPH must sufficiently correspond to one or more of those claims indicated as allowable (patentable) by the OEE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient correspondence is defined accounting for translation and claim format differences: claims are the same scope if they present the same technical features that made the OEE claims allowable; similar scope if differences are solely due to translation or claim format and do not deviate from original disclosure; narrower if the DPMA claim is further limited by an additional feature supported in the specification. A claim that introduces a new/different category of claims compared to those indicated as allowable by the OEE is not considered to sufficiently correspond (example: OEE only has process-of-manufacturing claims; DPMA adds product claims dependent on those process claims — not sufficient). 'Claim format' refers to the formal version of the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement d) DPMA has not begun substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The DPMA must not have begun substantive examination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely, the DPMA must not yet have sent a first office action (Erstbescheid) to the applicant after the request for examination. If substantive examination has begun (first office action issued), the PPH request is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission must use DPMA PPH request form and may be in German; incorporation by reference allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant has to file a request for accelerated examination under the PPH to the DPMA in German language by submitting a request form for accelerated examination under the PPH pilot programme accompanied by the relevant supporting documents. If the applicant has already submitted the documents indicated in 4a) to d) to the DPMA through simultaneous or past procedures, the applicant can incorporate the documents by reference and does not have to attach them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is available for download from the DPMA website. The form should be sent to the DPMA along with supporting documentation (or incorporate by reference when previously filed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable languages and translation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: With regard to the required documents, German, English and French are acceptable languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the available (machine) translation is insufficient, the DPMA examiner may request an additional translation from the applicant. Thus applicants may submit in DE/EN/FR but should be prepared to provide better translations on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document a) Copy of all OEE office actions (or listing if available online)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of all office actions on the corresponding OEE application(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions include: (a) decision to grant a patent, (b) first/second/third… and any further office action, (c) decision of refusal, (d) reexamination decision, and (e) invalidation decision. If these documents are available from an OEE online database (Patent Search and Service System of the CNIPA), the applicant does not have to submit them and only has to list the names of the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document b) Copy of the claims found patentable by the OEE (or listing if available online)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the claims found to be patentable by the OEE where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no need to submit a copy of the claims if they are available from an OEE online database (Patent Search and Service System of the CNIPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document c) Completed claim correspondence table
rubrics_metrics.description: A completed claim correspondence table showing the relationship between the claims of the DPMA application for accelerated examination under the PPH and the claims of the corresponding OEE application considered patentable by the OEE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient correspondence of claims occurs where the claims are of such a scope as defined under requirement 3c. When claims are literally translated, the applicant can simply write 'they are the same' in the table. When claims are not just literally translated, the applicant is allowed to explain the sufficient correspondence of each claim based on the criteria under 3c. In all cases of doubt the examiner may request an explanation of each claim based on 3c; otherwise the claims are presumed to correspond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required document d) Copies of documents cited by the OEE examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the document(s) cited by the OEE examiner must be provided where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the cited document is a patent document it does not have to be submitted as it is generally available to the DPMA via DEPATIS or EPOQUE. Where the DPMA has difficulty in obtaining a patent document it will ask the applicant to submit it. As a rule, cited documents need not be translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure outcome and resubmission/correction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requirements are met, the DPMA will conduct an accelerated examination. If the application does not qualify, the applicant will be informed and the application will be processed under the standard DPMA examination procedure, without acceleration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not meet all requirements, the applicant may correct defects and resubmit the PPH request. Before the issuing of the notification of not approving accelerated examination under the PPH pilot programme, the applicant may submit missing documents. Even after issuance of a notification of not approving accelerated examination, the applicant may file another PPH request so long as the request is filed before the issuing of the first office action. In other words, missing documents can be supplied and subsequent PPH requests filed up until the DPMA issues the first substantive office action.
